key_insight: The paper shows that open-ended LLM tasks can be converted into self-verifiable training problems, enabling RL-style self-improvement beyond domains with built-in correctness checks.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable way to train reasoning and generation models without relying on costly human labels, reward models, or LLM judges.
method: Transforms open-ended tasks into proxy environments with automatic reward signals.
Introduces SpyRL, a multi-agent self-play setup inspired by Who Is the Spy?
Uses asymmetric information and voting outcomes to create fully verifiable rewards.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on text summarization, creative writing, and mathematical reasoning, with SpyRL outperforming prior self-improvement methods on non-verifiable tasks and improving verifiable reasoning tasks as well.
watch_item: Proxy-task rewards may not perfectly align with the original task objective, so reward design and task transformation need careful validation.
paper_title: From RLVR to RLSVR: Task Transformation Induces Self-Verifiable Rewards for Open-Ended LLM Self-Improvement
